lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Check that the code link points directly to a polished, relevant portfolio or repository.
items.because: The résumé gives no other way to inspect your work.

items.says: Consider adding one directly relevant coursework, thesis, or research item to Education.
items.because: It may add value if it is worth the space.

items.says: Define diagnostic accuracy, its comparison point and evaluation scope, and whether 35% is relative or percentage-point improvement.
items.because: The outcome is not sufficiently interpretable.

items.says: Define reviewer disagreement and say whether the change is in percentage points or relative percent.
items.because: A reader may wonder how disagreement was measured.

items.says: Give the test volume or evaluation conditions behind the equal-accuracy comparison.
items.because: The comparison needs a credible evaluation basis.

items.says: Prioritize the tool-call reduction and maintained accuracy if those are better substantiated than the latency result.
items.because: The latency reduction is modest.

items.says: Clarify when the two regressions were caught and what kind they were.
items.because: That would make the evaluation-harness result more specific.

items.says: Consider moving this bullet higher in the internship entry.
items.because: Evaluation engineering may be central to the target roles.

items.says: The assistant-only loss-masking work overlaps with the first internship bullet.
items.because: The same method is presented as two separate achievements without a clear distinction.

items.says: The backlog reduction and sensor-signal count appear again under Projects.
items.because: The entries do not establish separate contributions.

items.says: Explain how the backlog reduction was calculated and, if possible, give the starting scale.
items.because: The impact needs more context.

items.says: Reorder the internship bullets after resolving duplication.
items.because: The strongest, most relevant evidence should appear first.

items.says: Make the meaning of the 4x memory reduction unambiguous.
items.because: “By 4x” can be interpreted inconsistently.

items.says: State whether the memory comparison used the same model, batch size, and training setup.
items.because: Those conditions affect how the reduction can be assessed.

items.says: Mention any effect on model quality or throughput, if applicable.
items.because: Those effects may matter alongside memory use.

items.says: Say whether the latency figures came from representative load tests or production traffic.
items.because: That would clarify the measurement basis.

items.says: The bullet switches from past tense to present tense at “adds.”
items.because: Its tense is inconsistent.

items.says: Clarify what a three-day release cycle measures and give the prior duration if it is a reduction.
items.because: The current phrasing does not establish the size of the improvement.

items.says: Quantify the backlogs or dispatch delays removed, if possible.
items.because: The operational result is meaningful but difficult to assess.

items.says: Replace or remove the broad claim about AI-first practices and downstream outcomes.
items.because: It gives no specific practice, adoption measure, delivery change, or downstream outcome.

items.says: Define the stress-test baseline, what the 100x growth compares, and successful context retention.
items.because: Without those details, the scale claim is hard to interpret.

items.says: Give the test conditions or failure rate demonstrating the concurrency fix, if available.
items.because: It is unclear whether 50-way fan-out was a stress test or a production workload.

items.says: Identify the evaluation framework if it is public.
items.because: The framework is not named.

items.says: Make ownership clearer than the “Contributor” label does.
items.because: The extent of your contribution is unclear.

items.says: Clarify whether your metrics work was merged, released, or used by others.
items.because: The outcome of the contribution is unclear.

items.says: Explain what was correlated and what the 400+ trials represent.
items.because: The result would be easier for technical reviewers and recruiters to understand.

items.says: The pending-case backlog result repeats the Mobility Systems Company achievement.
items.because: A reader is likely to count it as the same result twice.

items.says: Consider adding other tools or languages used in the listed work when relevant to target jobs.
items.because: They may be useful skills that the section does not show.

items.says: Organize the skills by function rather than mixing modeling, agent evaluation, and Kubernetes.
items.because: The grouping is harder to scan.

items.says: Support Kubernetes with meaningful experience or project evidence.
items.because: It currently has little supporting context in the bullets.

items.says: Make “agent evaluation” more specific if you have particular methods or tooling to name.
items.because: The term is broad.

items.says: Consider a brief target-role summary or headline.
items.because: Without one, readers must infer the intended role from the experience.

items.says: Make individual scope clearer in team-based accomplishments.
items.because: The résumé often does not say what you personally designed, implemented, or evaluated.

items.says: Make production deployment scope clearer.
items.because: The résumé does not establish that scope for qualification screening.
